prompt.es: Caso final: escribe tu respuesta integrada (unas 170 palabras).

answer.text: Years ago, I used to believe that I would never speak English well. I had never spoken with a stranger in English, and I was afraid of making mistakes. Then I started studying with an app every morning, and my confidence slowly grew. The article says that students who learn with apps never speak well. Admittedly, an app alone may not be enough: it cannot give you a real conversation. Much as I respect the author, I would argue that the claim is too strong. The source seems to rely on a small survey, and it gives no data about students who also talk with people, so its conclusion may not be reliable. I was wondering whether the author could explain how many students took part. I understand that a short article has little space, and I appreciate the concern about speaking well. Revision: I wrote that apps are useless for speaking, or rather, I should say that they are useful but not enough. On balance, the best plan is an app plus real conversations, and that is exactly what this course has given me.
accepted: Years ago, I used to believe that I would never speak English well. I had never spoken with a stranger in English, and I was afraid of making mistakes. Then I started studying with an app every morning, and my confidence slowly grew. The article says that students who learn with apps never speak well. Admittedly, an app alone may not be enough: it cannot give you a real conversation. Much as I respect the author, I would argue that the claim is too strong. The source seems to rely on a small survey, and it gives no data about students who also talk with people, so its conclusion may not be reliable. I was wondering whether the author could explain how many students took part. I understand that a short article has little space, and I appreciate the concern about speaking well. Revision: I wrote that apps are useless for speaking, or rather, I should say that they are useful but not enough. On balance, the best plan is an app plus real conversations, and that is exactly what this course has given me.

When I was a child, I would watch films in English without understanding a word, and my cousin used to laugh at me. Later, I had to take an exam, and that was the moment when I decided to learn properly. An online post claims that apps are a waste of time. It is true that an app cannot replace a teacher. Even though I agree with part of that view, I think the post may be wrong, because it gives no numbers and does not say who wrote it. The source seems weak, so I would be careful before believing it. I was wondering whether the author has ever used an app for a full year. With respect, one experience does not prove a rule. I appreciate that some people learn better with a teacher, and I see your point. Let me rephrase my conclusion: apps do not teach everything, but they help you to start. In the end, I changed my opinion only a little, and this course helped me to explain why.

feedback.es: El caso final integra antecedente, argumento con concesión, evaluación cautelosa de la fuente, tacto y una revisión documentada.

origin.text: Un artículo afirma: «Los estudiantes que aprenden inglés con apps nunca llegan a hablar con fluidez.» Responde: cuenta un antecedente personal con tiempos coherentes; argumenta con concesión y refutación matizada; evalúa la fuente con cautela; muestra tacto ante quien piensa distinto; y termina documentando una revisión (or rather…).
